scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements, dimensions, tolerances, chemical compositions, mechanical properties, and performance-testing schedules for seamless, solid drawn phosphorized deoxidized copper (Cu-DHP) tubes designed for plumbing and sanitation applications [1, 2]. These tubes are suitable for general plumbing, domestic hot/cold water supply, drainage, and similar piping systems for the conveyance of fluids, commonly jointed using solder, flared, or compression-type fittings [1].

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Metallurgical Engineering / Domestic Piping Infrastructure)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Copper Products (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), Government of India, all copper tubes for plumbing must conform to IS 14810:2000 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Enforcement began on October 19, 2024, for medium and large-scale enterprises, January 19, 2025, for small enterprises, and April 19, 2025, for micro enterprises. Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified plumbing tubes is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial plumbing copper tubes.

requirements.detail: Every commercial package or tube length of plumbing pipe must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard reference to verify compliance.

The tubes must be manufactured from Grade Cu-DHP (Phosphorized deoxidized copper with high residual phosphorus) conforming to IS 191 (Part 8), ensuring a minimum copper purity of 99.90 percent (including silver) and phosphorus content restricted to between 0.015 and 0.040 percent [1]. This composition prevents hydrogen embrittlement and maintains long-term structural toughness.

Plumbing tubes must be manufactured through a solid drawing process (seamless construction). Longitudinal welding is strictly prohibited to guarantee maximum pressure handling, leak tightness, and high resistance to splitting.

Tubes must be cut to size in coils or straight lengths, properly drafted, and securely sealed at both ends. This sealing prevents dirt, moisture, and microbial contaminants from entering the tube bore during transit and storage.

The inner and outer surfaces of the tubes must be clean, bright, smooth, and completely free from harmful defects such as deep scratches, cracks, inclusions, pitting, or visible oxidation scale, with the bore entirely free from deleterious residue films.

Every single tube length must withstand a standard hydrostatic test pressure calculated per formula: P = (2 * F * t) / (D - t)
where P is pressure (MPa), t is wall thickness (mm), D is outside diameter (mm), and F is design stress (72.5 MPa for HD, 60.0 MPa for HB, and 46.0 MPa for O condition). The tube must sustain this pressure for at least 5 seconds with zero leakage or sweating.

Consignments of identical diameters, thicknesses, and tempers are grouped into inspection lots of 300 tubes or 1,000 kg (whichever is greater). One random sample tube is tested per lot. If it fails, two retest tubes are drawn. If both retests pass, the lot is accepted; if either fails, the entire lot is rejected.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 14810 : 2000 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing solid drawn (seamless) phosphorized deoxidized copper (Cu-DHP) tubes used in residential, commercial, and industrial plumbing systems for carrying hot and cold water, drainage, and other plumbing fluids [1]. Under India's statutory Copper Products Quality Control Order (QCO), all copper plumbing tubes must conform to this standard and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to guarantee water safety, leak tightness, and pressure handling. The standard classifies tubes across four sizing charts based on temper (annealed, half-hard, and hard drawn), covering outside diameters from micro-bore 6 mm up to 159 mm [2, 3]. It enforces detailed physical and mechanical requirements—including minimum tensile strength (210 to 310 MPa), high elongation (up to 40%), drift expansion flares without splitting, and 100% leak-proof hydrostatic pressure tests calculated using grade-specific design stresses [3].
